name: Fontainebleau Las Vegas
desc: Luxury 3,644-room casino resort on the Las Vegas Strip opened in December 2023 by Jeffrey Soffer's Fontainebleau Development.
products: Casino, hotel, dining, nightlife, convention space
customers: Premium Las Vegas visitors and groups
minority_investors: Koch Real Estate Investments partnered on the 2021 purchase
markets: Las Vegas; sister Fontainebleau Miami Beach

fit_rationale: Fontainebleau already sold a Las Vegas Grand Prix luxury package in 2024; a deeper race or team deal suits its non-gaming luxury positioning on the Strip.
category_conflict: potential: MGM Resorts, Caesars, Wynn, The Venetian hold F1 deals; check whether a 2025-26 Las Vegas GP deal exists
outstanding: No revenue or equity figure found; USD 3.7bn project cost not usable as equity; check for a current Las Vegas Grand Prix deal.

name: 1/ST (The Stronach Group)
desc: Thoroughbred racing and pari-mutuel wagering group owning Santa Anita and Gulfstream Park, Xpressbet, AmTote and 1/ST TV.
products: Racetracks, account wagering (Xpressbet), totalisator systems (AmTote), racing media (1/ST TV)
customers: US racing bettors; racetracks using AmTote systems
stores_or_sites: Santa Anita Park, Gulfstream Park, Laurel Park (closing after 2026 Preakness), Rosecroft Raceway
markets: United States (California, Florida, Maryland); HQ Canada

signals.what: Agreed sale of Preakness Stakes rights to Churchill Downs; Maryland matched and acquired the rights

fit_rationale: Gulfstream Park sits near the Miami Grand Prix; cross-promotion of the Pegasus World Cup with Miami race week is plausible, but the group is shrinking its Maryland assets.
